label: culture-new-factcheck-codex-20261012-v2
review_type: independent finite fact/options and learning-value review

scope.v1_blinding: No fully blind claim: the previous review disclosed its accidental article preview before the candidate-first check. This v2 review evaluates the frozen revised draft.

batch_verdict.reason: All twelve answer keys and stated core facts checked against the cited Academy/Recording Academy sources, but this is not yet the varied, educational culture batch requested. Seven stems are award/nomination/category prompts (05–07 and 09–12), including five direct nomination/statistic lookups (05, 06, 09, 11, 12). Three questions reuse the same 65th-Grammy record, and two each reuse Gandhi/1983 and Raging Bull/1981. Every article spends the identical 29-word closing paragraph telling the learner how to inspect source cards, leaving 92–100 non-template body words; that is mechanically padded rather than film/music learning. Rewrite as concise, useful 60–100-word factual mini-articles, extending only where a source-rich claim earns the additional length, and remove all how-to-consult-source or guessing-answer filler.

structural_checks.answer_length_or_parenthesis_giveaway: No positional, parenthetical, or conspicuously longer-key giveaway found. v2-02 nevertheless has an invented/opaque distractor, Jacob Rimiss, rather than four comparably plausible names.
structural_checks.cross_question_spoilers: No article states another item's exact answer. Context clustering still reduces variety: 01/06 Gandhi (1983); 02/03 Raging Bull (1981); 09/11/12 65th Grammys (2023).
structural_checks.existing_quiz_duplicate_check: Searched all quizzes/**/*.json for every revised title/name. Only a semantic near-duplicate was found: quizzes/Preparation/prep_film_directors_1.json asks who directed Raging Bull and explains Jake LaMotta. v2-02 uses the same film/person connection, so it should be replaced or moved to a materially different learning objective. The remaining searched terms had no literal match.

source_review.availability: All opened cited sources returned usable official content except the supplied 2003/Z?qt-honorees=1 URL, which timed out. The Academy base 2003 page opened and confirms the relevant credits, so replace the unstable URL rather than retaining it.
source_review.breadth_and_derived_content: There are no science questions. Academy and Recording Academy records are primary for the award/credit metadata, but they cannot turn award-list recall into a broad film/music learning article. The repetitive 29-word source-reading boilerplate is not source-derived. Conservative manual estimates of source-derived fact paraphrase per repeatedly used official page are below 200 words (about 101 for 1983, 97 for 1981, and 110 for the 65th Grammys); this is an estimate, not a copyright measurement. Use a substantive film-credit, editing, songwriting, or production source before retaining craft exposition.

questions.correction: Keep the crew-role premise, but replace the generic award-card tutorial and shared closing with sourced facts about this production. Do not use 55th-ceremony metadata as most of the lesson.

questions.key_check: PASS — Robert De Niro played Jake LaMotta; the Academy 1981 material supports the actor/film/boxer link.
questions.correction: Replace Jacob Rimiss with a real, plausible boxer or Raging Bull figure, and replace the item because an existing quiz already asks the Raging Bull director and explains Jake LaMotta. Remove the generic source-card closing.

questions.key_check: PASS — Thelma Schoonmaker won Film Editing for Raging Bull.
questions.correction: The Academy pages substantiate the credit, not the broad definition of what an editor does. Cite a real editing/craft source and explain a concrete editorial choice, or replace the explanatory claims; also avoid the second item on the same film.

questions.correction: Replace the timed-out /2003/Z?qt-honorees=1 link with /2003. Replace the generic adapted-screenplay/award-card lesson and repeated closing with a specific, source-backed fact about adapting Szpilman's memoir.

questions.correction: Replace with a film-performance or production fact. It is exact but remains a rare-nomination-statistic lookup, and the article teaches how to parse award status rather than about either film.

questions.correction: Replace the numeric award-count recall. It repeats v2-01's Gandhi/1983 source context and its explanation is largely generic instructions plus a count.

questions.correction: Retain the songwriter-versus-recording insight, but ask it without making the category page the subject and teach a concrete credit distinction. Remove the generic closing.

questions.correction: This is the strongest non-award premise, but the article's broad credit-role statements need a music-production source or a direct, album-specific credit fact. Make every distractor genuinely album-adjacent and remove the repeated closing.

questions.correction: Replace the direct nominee-list lookup. If Oasis remains in any rewrite, describe it accurately as a Bad Bunny/J Balvin collaborative album rather than implying every option is a solo Bad Bunny album.

questions.correction: Keep the useful composer/lyricist/performer distinction, but reframe it as a film-music credit question with a source about the song's creation, rather than another Grammy result. Remove the generic closing.

questions.correction: Replace this nominee/category lookup, especially because v2-09 and v2-12 already use the same ceremony. Use an artist, song, or production fact with an explanation that teaches it.
